public_rationale: The preprint submitted March 4, 2024 evaluates ChatGPT-assisted game design through prototypes and participant feedback [e1]. It examines creative behavior, but does not test whether dataset training confers lived experience or responsibility for production [e1]. Its results cannot settle the combined assertion about creative ability, experience and responsibility [e1].
limitations: The statement does not distinguish observable adaptation and judgment from responsibility and lived experience, or define a measurable standard for the combined claim.
The wording does not distinguish current limitations from an inherent impossibility.
Benefits or shortcomings in the game-design study establish neither acquisition of all these qualities nor their untrainability [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The adaptability, judgment and responsibility of human creative workers cannot be trained into AI via datasets.

statement.excerpt: These are not things that you can train in a dataset, because they're derived from experiences inside and outside of the creative process.

from_speaker: not things that you can train in a dataset

our_interpretation: The referent combines observable creative behavior, human experience, and responsibility for production.
A narrower claim about responding to feedback could be tested. Treating that narrower capability as equivalent to the entire statement would omit its central responsibility and experience components.
The wording also leaves unresolved whether it describes current limitations or an inherent impossibility of dataset training.
criteria.support_condition: No single empirical support condition fairly covers the statement as written. Poor performance by particular systems would not establish that these qualities cannot be trained.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No single empirical contradiction condition fairly covers the statement as written. Successful creative revisions would test a behavioral component but would not establish transferred responsibility or human experience.
